subject: Carve-out request: filter & toolchain failures impacting structured outputs (Acme PoC)
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme-inc.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:14:02 -0700
Subject: Unexpected structured-output failures during PoC — asking for carve-out

Hi Grace,

Quick note from our QA team: during two PoC runs last week we saw the agent return an empty JSON payload or a truncated object when the content filter triggered on certain user inputs. The UX shows 'no answer' and our downstream pipelines mark the row as failed. I've attached a sanitized error trace.

This behavior only happens when a tool call or structured response is blocked by the filter, and it materially impacts our throughput for the PoC. Given the production SLA language in the draft, Procurement asked whether Redwood can provide an exclusion for filter-induced non-deliveries (i.e. cases where the model attempted the call but a safety rule prevented a valid structured response).

Can you point me to how you treat these incidents in uptime calculations and whether you can offer language for a carve-out or alternate remediation (credits/fallbacks)? Happy to jump on a quick call — we have a tight deadline for procurement next week.

Thanks,
Maria Gomez
Director, AI Integrations
Acme, Inc.
[Attachment: acme-filter-error-sample-20270411.txt (text)]
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme-inc.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:03:21 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected structured-output failures during PoC — asking for carve-out

Hi Maria — thanks for the example and flag. Looping in Rishi (platform) and Lauren (account lead) to outline options.

Short answer: we treat policy-triggered non-deliveries differently from runtime outages today, but we don't have a standard customer-facing carve-out in every contract. We can draft specific language for the Acme PoC that: 1) documents the conditions that qualify (policy-triggered filtering or tool-call suppression), 2) excludes those events from the uptime calculation, and 3) prescribes remediation (structured-logging, alerting, and optional credit or extended trial).

Before I draft, two quick Qs:
- Is Acme looking for an exclusion only during the PoC, or for production contract language?
- Are there specific business metrics you want protected (e.g., percentage of successful structured responses vs. absolute uptime)?

Happy to do a short call tomorrow.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0132
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:27:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected structured-output failures during PoC — asking for carve-out

Hi team — technical context that should shape the carve-out language:

1) Failure class: these incidents are 'policy suppressions' where a safety filter prevents a tool invocation or structured-output formatter from returning the expected payload. The model runtime is not down; instead the request is intentionally blocked.

2) Detectability: we can surface a specific signal in logs (policy.suppressed=true) and emit a tracing tag so Acme can distinguish these from genuine runtime errors. We'll provide an example log schema.

3) Mitigation options: the platform can (a) route to a lower sensitivity policy variant, (b) return a standardized error object that downstream code can handle, or (c) fall back to a sanitized textual response instead of returning an empty payload. Each has different risk profiles.

4) Proposed SLA treatment: exclude incidents from uptime where the root cause is policy suppression AND we have a corresponding trace/log entry plus a confirmed opt-in from the customer to accept policy-exclusion handling for that workload.

5) Suggested remediation commitments for the PoC: we can guarantee 1) structured logs for every suppression event sent to Acme's logging endpoint, 2) an agreed fallback behavior (we recommend standardized error object + telemetry), and 3) a weekly summary of suppression events during the PoC.

I'll attach a short technical appendix for the log fields and a draft snippet for contract language.

- Rishi
Principal Platform Engineer
[Attachment: redwood-filter-suppression-log-schema-v1.txt (text)]
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:12:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected structured-output failures during PoC — asking for carve-out

Thoughts on risk/wording from legal ops POV (draft bullets to include in Grace's reply to Acme):

- Scope: carve-out applies only to incidents where a policy evaluation deterministically prevented a tool-call or structured-output from being returned. It does not apply to server outages, degraded latency, or SDK failures.
- Evidence: each event must include a policy.suppressed trace id and the raw (redacted) input for audit. We commit to delivering that evidence within 48 hours of request.
- Mitigation: Redwood will implement a standardized error object and provide a recommended fallback mapping to help Acme's integration avoid downstream failures.
- Duration & opt-in: carve-out is configurable per-environment. For the PoC, Acme can opt-in for the duration of the pilot; production language to be negotiated.
- Credits: because policy suppression is intentional, we propose not to issue uptime credits for these events, but instead to provide operational counters + a 1-week extension on the PoC if suppression rates exceed a threshold (e.g., >0.5% of calls).

If you want, I can turn these bullets into a one-paragraph contract amendment and attach the redline.

-Karthik
Director, Legal Ops
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme-inc.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme-inc.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 17:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed carve-out & operational commitments for PoC — Acme

Hi Maria / Acme procurement team — thanks again for the sample logs and for raising this. Attached is a short amendment (v1) proposing clear criteria and operational commitments for the PoC. High level summary:

- Scope: Events where Redwood's safety/policy evaluation deliberately suppresses a tool call or structured response will be excluded from the PoC uptime calculation, provided Acme opts in for the workload.
- Evidence & telemetry: Redwood will emit a policy.suppressed trace id for each event, deliver structured logs to your logging endpoint, and provide a weekly suppression summary.
- Mitigation: Redwood will implement the standardized error object fallback for the PoC and offer a secondary lower-sensitivity policy profile as an opt-in. We will not silently change policy levels without written consent.
- Financials & credits: In lieu of uptime credits for policy-suppression events, Redwood proposes a 7-day PoC extension if suppression rate exceeds 0.5% of requests over a 7-day window.
- Timing & acceptance: We can enable telemetry and the error-object fallback within 48–72 hours of Acme's confirmation. Amendment attached for review. If this looks good, please indicate acceptance and we will generate a short DocuSign.

Next steps we suggest: 1) Proc to confirm opt-in for PoC carve-out, 2) Tech Ops confirm logging endpoint and event schema, 3) Redwood enables fallback and schedules a short runbook review with Acme engineers.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-proposed-carveout-amendment-v1.pdf (pdf)]
